newsitem.title: USA: NYS exempts Internet access firms from sales tax.
newsitem.headline: NYS exempts Internet access firms from sales tax.

text.p: New York State Gov George Pataki on Friday directed the state tax department to exempt Internet access service from sales taxes, as part of his effort to boost employment in the new industry.

The state tax department conducted a year-long study, required by 1995 legislation, on issues posed by the Internet, which was submitted to the governor on Friday by Taxation and Finance Commissioner Michael Urbach.
The report also concluded that because Internet access services were not telecommnications, their receipts were outside the scope of the Section 186-3 gross receipts excise tax.

The state will not collect sales taxes from out-of-state or non-U.S. firms that advertise on the Internet through a New York-based access provider, a decision designed to make such firms more attractive to such entities.

"New York is the first state in the nation to take this bold step," Pataki said, in prepared remarks. "We have improved our competitive edge as we compete with places like Seattle and Silcon Valley in California for Internet-related jobs."
